sources.title: GTA 6 Is Now Available to Pre-Load on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S
sources.text: The day has come: if you’ve preordered Grand Theft Auto 6 , you can now preload the game onto your PS5 or Xbox Series X|S. You’ll need 212GB of space on your drive , but if you have the free storage space, you can load the game onto your console so it’s ready to go when it releases on November 19 (you can check your global release time here ). If you preordered a "physical copy," you’ll have to wait until it arrives to preload it, but it should be delivered within the next few days. I use scare quotes on the words "physical copy" because there is no actual disc version of GTA 6. Physical copies are simply a box that includes a code you can redeem on the PlayStation Store or Xbox Store. Those who haven’t preordered a copy can do so now and begin their preload. It’s available in two editions: standard and ultimate. The ultimate edition comes with a bunch of extra in-game digital items, detailed below. Physical copies of GTA 6 are only available for the standard edition. But, if you want a box to put on your shelf and you also want the ultimate edition, you can buy the physical standard edition, and then buy the "Ultimate Edition Upgrade," which basically turns your standard edition into the ultimate edition. The total cost is the same. Here are all the preorder links you'll need, in case you haven't locked in your preorder yet but want to jump on it now that preloads are live. Grand Theft Auto VI is now confirmed as the most pre-ordered game in history on both the PlayStation Store (according to the official PlayStation Blog ) and the Microsoft Store (according to Microsoft's official Xbox Wire ). That's perhaps unsurprising, both because it's probably the most highly anticipated game ever released, and because physical copies only exist in "code in a box" form. Even so, it's impressive. The Vintage Vice City Pack is included with all digital purchases of GTA 6 made prior to November 20, 2026, and with preorders of the physical version of GTA 6 while supplies last. Jason: An effortlessly chic linen suit in vintage pastel, complemented by the cut and coif of the decade of decadence. Lucia: The world is yours in a red sequin mini dress and curls. sources.text: Rockstar divulga trailer de lançamento de GTA 6! Assista novo vídeo legendado em PT-BR O momento mais aguardado pelos fãs de videogames nos últimos dez anos está cada vez mais próximo. Strauss Zelnick, CEO da Take-Two, confirmou na teleconferência mais recente da publisher que o desenvolvimento de GTA 6 foi concluído e o jogo está pronto para o lançamento . A partir de agora, a Rockstar Games deve concentrar seus esforços no refinamento da experiência e na preparação de uma possível atualização de primeiro dia. Além disso, o pré-load de GTA 6 também já está disponível no PS5 e no Xbox Series X|S , inclusive no Brasil. A Rockstar concluiu o desenvolvimento da versão principal de GTA 6 e concedeu ao projeto o famigerado status “Gold”. Na indústria de games, isso significa que a versão final destinada à distribuição foi oficialmente concluída e a etapa principal de desenvolvimento chegou ao fim. Normalmente, o anúncio de que um jogo atingiu esse estágio acontece semanas antes do lançamento, já que as empresas precisam preparar cópias físicas, embalagens e a distribuição para lojas — mesmo que o conteúdo da mídia física seja apenas um código digital. “Neste momento, a Rockstar concluiu o desenvolvimento de GTA 6”, confirmou Zelnick na teleconferência de resultados da última segunda (09), reiterando que a Rockstar fez “o seu melhor trabalho até agora”. Como a distribuição digital não depende do envio de discos para fábricas, a Rockstar pode concentrar os preparativos na versão digital e na infraestrutura da PlayStation Network. Informações sobre os arquivos hospedados na rede da Sony também indicam que a estrutura de distribuição do jogo já está preparada. O status Gold, no entanto, não significa que todo o trabalho terminou. A equipe ainda pode desenvolver uma atualização de primeiro dia, realizar testes nos servidores e corrigir possíveis problemas antes da estreia. Além disso, o marco não elimina completamente a possibilidade de mudanças no cronograma de lançamento. Vale lembrar também que o pré-carregamento de GTA 6 já começou no PS5 e no Xbox Series X|S , permitindo que os jogadores baixem os arquivos antes da estreia. Segundo a Rockstar, o download no PS5 e no Xbox Series X|S começou à meia-noite desta terça (10), seguindo o horário local de cada região. Quem comprou GTA 6 digitalmente pode configurar o console para realizar o download automaticamente. No PS5, é necessário ativar os downloads automáticos e deixar o aparelho ligado ou em modo de repouso. Já no Xbox, o procedimento envolve habilitar as atualizações automáticas e manter o console ligado ou em modo de suspensão. A PlayStation recomenda que os jogadores liberem pelo menos 212 GB de espaço no armazenamento do PS5 antes de iniciar o download. Depois do pré-load, será possível acessar o jogo a partir da meia-noite de 19 de novembro, conforme o horário local, tanto no console da Sony quanto nos aparelhos da Microsoft. Claro, a pré-venda de GTA 6 segue disponível , com duas versões do jogo oferecidas nas plataformas — além da versão física sem disco que gerou polêmicas na comunidade . sources.text: O pré-download de Grand Theft Auto VI ( GTA 6 ) já está disponível para PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X|S . sources.text: With no PC port in sight, prospective GTA 6 players need to decide between the PS5 and XBOX Series X|S. Each console has different specs and features to consider. Data shows that GTA 6 is the most pre-ordered game ever . The majority are on PS5, but not all of them. Even people who aren’t gamers are jumping at the chance to play GTA 6, which is where the PS5 versus XBOX Series X|S debate comes into play. Also, you can buy Grand Theft Auto 6 here , if you haven’t already! To start, we’re going to run through the respective key default specs for the XBOX Series X model, and the standard PS5 and PS5 Pro variant. The PlayStation 5 Pro is the most powerful current-gen console to play GTA 6 on . For base models, the XBOX Series X|S takes the crown over the normal PS5. However, since the Series X|S doesn’t have a Pro version, the actual overall winner is the PS5 Pro. The Pro has the most powerful hardware and the best features, but it comes with a slight caveat: The price. The base PS5 costs $649.99, whereas you’re looking at $799.99 for the XBOX Series X|S. However, if you want a PS5 Pro, it’ll cost you $899. The RAM Crisis and other operational costs have seen Sony and Microsoft increase console prices instead of the traditional decrease as console lifecycles advance. In my opinion, PlayStation is the best place to enjoy Grand Theft Auto 6, but the debate about the base PS5 and PS5 Pro is a bit tougher where GTA is concerned. If you’re upgrading to current-gen and you only care about having the best GTA 6 experience possible, then it’s recommended you go all out and buy the PS5 Pro. It also means that any subsequent games you buy will be enjoyed best on the console, and the AI-based PSSR (PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution) is a juicy graphical improvement for applicable games. Crédito: Voxl A Rockstar Games anunciou nesta segunda-feira (9) a realização do Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival , evento musical especial inspirado no universo de GTA 6. O festival acontecerá no dia 21 de novembro de 2026 , no espaço Mana Wynwood, em Miami, nos Estados Unidos, e contará com apresentações de artistas como Travis Scott, Cardi B, Justice e Metro Boomin. O evento foi organizado para celebrar o lançamento de Grand Theft Auto VI e reunirá músicos presentes no jogo e em sua trilha sonora oficial. A programação terá dois palcos com apresentações ao longo do festival, incluindo shows e sets de DJs. A iniciativa é uma parceria entre Rockstar Games e PlayStation, com produção dos responsáveis pelo festival III Points. A entrada será permitida apenas para maiores de 17 anos, e os ingressos serão distribuídos por meio de um sorteio, com inscrições abertas no site oficial do evento. A programação do Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival reúne nomes de diferentes estilos musicais, passando pelo hip-hop, música eletrônica e ritmos latinos, seguindo os padrões das rádios do game . Um dos destaques será a apresentação especial da Cactus Jack, gravadora e selo musical de Travis Scott, que também contará com Don Toliver, Kodak Black e Sofaygo. Confira a lista completa de artistas confirmados: A seleção reforça a importância da música na identidade de GTA 6, que terá Vice City como um dos principais cenários. A trilha sonora é uma parte tradicional da franquia, com estações de rádio, músicas licenciadas e artistas que ajudam a construir a personalidade de cada cidade. Os ingressos para o evento serão vendidos por meio de uma loteria organizada pela plataforma DICE, com códigos exclusivos enviados pelo serviço Laylo. Os interessados precisam se inscrever no sorteio pelo site oficial do festival . O prazo para participar termina em 10 de novembro, às 16h (horário de Brasília). Cada comprador poderá adquirir até dois ingressos, que não poderão ser transferidos para outras pessoas. A organização também recomenda criar uma conta na DICE utilizando o mesmo e-mail e telefone informados durante a inscrição na loteria, evitando que a participação seja identificada como atividade de bots. O Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival acontecerá no Mana Wynwood, localizado no endereço 318 NW 23rd St, em Miami. A organização recomenda utilizar serviços de transporte por aplicativo, já que o espaço não terá estacionamento próprio e as vagas disponíveis nas proximidades serão administradas por terceiros. Além da exigência de idade mínima de 17 anos, o evento terá regras específicas de segurança e acesso. Todos os participantes passarão por revistas, incluindo inspeção de bolsas e pertences pessoais, e não será permitida a entrada com alimentos, bebidas, armas, drones ou equipamentos profissionais de gravação. A organização também divulgou orientações de acessibilidade, incluindo áreas reservadas para pessoas com deficiência e a possibilidade de solicitar pulseiras especiais gratuitamente no local. O festival em Miami amplia essa proposta para além dos videogames, levando parte da identidade musical de GTA 6 para um evento presencial. sources.text: How far would you travel to make it to the GTA 6 festival? Just when you thought the celebrations for Grand Theft Auto 6 couldn't get any more extravagant, Rockstar has announced that it will be hosting a huge music festival in Miami just a few days after its release. But that begs the question: who's going to turn up? I thought everyone was going to be playing GTA 6 ? "Experience the music of Vice City and Leonida at Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival, a special live event on November 21 at Mana Wynwood in Miami to celebrate the launch of GTAVI, featuring a star-studded lineup of artists from the game and the official soundtrack," an official blog post reads. The event is in partnership with PlayStation and will feature "two stages of nonstop music performances" with the following artists: Tickets will be available via a lottery system for those aged 17+ with exclusive codes being sent out to those who managed to win a spot when the entries are drawn on today at 4 pm ET/ 9 pm GMT. But there are a couple things to keep in mind. There's no word on how expensive the tickets will be, with prices likely being revealed later today in the lottery, and the festival is a mere two weeks away, as it takes place on November 21, 2026. So, unless you're a super fan with money to spare on not only a festival ticket but also a last-minute plane ticket to Miami, this event will likely be for locals or, at the very least, those already in the US. My only issue is that if you're so big a fan that you're willing to drop everything last minute and head over to Florida then why aren't you actually playing GTA 6? The festival is happening just two days after GTA 6, I'm pretty sure we're all busy around then. sources.title: GTA 6 Caused Some Gamers to Hold Off on Buying New Games — Including Take-Two's Own NBA 2K27, Strauss Zelnick Says
sources.text: The behemoth that is GTA 6 looms large over the video game industry, and it’s so big that it not only caused the September crush of releases, but caused some gamers to hold off on buying new games. Reporting its latest financial results, Take-Two, parent company of GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games, said that its own NBA 2K27 had sold 4 million units, which was “below our forecast for the period.” Take-Two, which owns both 2K and NBA developer Visual Concepts, said that the NBA 2K27 launch window was “unusually busy, with numerous entertainment experiences competing for players’ attention.” In an accompanying interview with IGN , Zelnick expanded on the point, adding that he felt that GTA 6 had an impact also. “I think the key point is that while below our forecast, NBA 2K27 is our second best release of NBA 2K in history. It's an immensely successful title. It sold 4 million units. And in launching more content than ever before for the rest of the year, we have expectations that the title will do even better than it already has done,” Zelnick began. “I do think that this timing may have affected performance so far. It has been a crowded period, and we do think that GTA 6 coming has had an influence on the consumer. That said, we're thrilled with how NBA 2K27 is performing.” GTA 6 is credited with forcing developers and publishers to either bring their releases forward or move them back in an effort to avoid November. The likes of The Blood of Dawn Walker, Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Marvel's Wolverine, Control Resonant and others all launched up against each other in September. NBA 2K27 was officially released globally on September 4, 2026. Based on Zelnick's comments, GTA 6 won't just have affected NBA 2K27 sales, but caused some gamers to skip other games in favor of Rockstar's next, which comes out November 19. It is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time, setting sales and revenue records, so Take-Two will of course be fine for some time to come. Other publishers and developers, though, might be left struggling. For now, though, during the quarter Take-Two saw revenue of $1.6 billion, which was slightly below its guidance range of $1.62-$1.67 billion. The company said fiscal 2027 will be "an historic year for Take-Two – driven by our unwavering commitment to delivering the highest quality entertainment experiences." sources.title: 'The experiences on console and PC tend to be roughly the same,' says Take-Two CEO in response to question about GTA roleplaying
sources.text: Of course, in the case of Grand Theft Auto 6, the PC experience at launch will be a blank screen. On a call with investors today , Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick pushed back on the idea that PC players have a different relationship with the Grand Theft Auto series than console players. "Your PC players seem to engage with GTA a bit differently than console," said Oppenheimer & Co analyst Martin Yang during a Q&A session. "There are roleplay options. Over time, do you think you want to close the player experience gap between console and PC, or do you view the two platforms as more independent because of their respective technical capabilities?" Zelnick responded with acknowledgement that series like Civilization started on PC and expanded onto consoles, but said that "generally speaking, the experiences on console and PC tend to be roughly the same" and that, in general, "the capabilities of the PC platform today aren't different materially from console capabilities." The vanilla GTA Online experience may be roughly equivalent for console and PC players, but the console versions don't have the mods that have helped keep GTA 5 relevant for 13 years. Take-Two of course knows that: It acquired the FiveM GTA 5 multiplayer mod behind so many RP servers. Answering a related question about console jailbreaking, modding, and monetization opportunities, Zelnick said later that "the FiveM business is a profitable business," but then turned back to one of his stock lines. "The mission of this company is to create the best entertainment on earth and bring it to consumers around the world," said the Take-Two CEO. "If we do that right, the monetization takes care of itself." Take-Two has consistently declined to reveal anything about its plans for GTA 6 on PC or the future of GTA Online, and I didn't have high hopes that it would change tack with the console launch just over a week away, but props to the savvy investment analysts who asked about the topics anyway. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. As I think the questioner from Oppenheimer was getting at, it's sensible to wonder whether the custom servers and roleplaying features made popular by GTA 5 modders and streamers on PC will come stock in the next GTA Online iteration, including on consoles. Zelnick didn't sound particularly enthused about modding in his responses today—he said that Take-Two "isn't religious on the topic"—but I'm not reading much into it. sources.title: GTA 6 pre-orders are ‘far above initial expectations’ but NBA 2K27 was ‘below our forecast’, Take-Two says
sources.text: NBA was still the second most successful launch in the series’ history, it says Take-Two says pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto 6 are “far above initial expectations”, but its other recent major release NBA 2K27 hasn’t met its forecast. Despite delivering “the second highest net bookings performance in the history of the series” and selling more than 4 million copies since its release in early September, NBA 2K27 “was below our forecast for the period”, according to the publisher. It expects big things from GTA 6 , however, stating: “Pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto VI are tracking far above our initial expectations, and we know that the numbers will speak for themselves soon enough.” Despite this claim, Take-Two has only modestly revised its forecast for the financial year, adjusting its range from $7.9 – $8.1 billion up to $7.98 – $8.18 billion. In an interview with GamesIndustry.biz, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said the company was not yet adjusting its guidance because the game is so close to release. “[We cannot] disclose the numbers, but the point that we’re making is our prior expectations obviously were aligned with our guidance, and the pre-orders are far exceeding our original expectations,” Zelnick said. “We’re maintaining our guidance, because the release is only 10 days away and we’ll know a lot more after the release.” When asked whether the decision to keep the guidance at around $8 billion for the year was a sign that Take-Two wasn’t predicting a bigger than expected launch, Zelnick reiterated: “We’re just not updating our numbers right now because we are so close to the launch. However, pre-orders are far exceeding our expectations.” Elsewhere in the interview, Zelnick was asked whether he felt the wave of live service games had passed. He replied that the vast majority of Take-Two’s income still comes from live service titles (such as GTA Online, NBA 2K or WWE 2K), the upcoming release of GTA aside. “We’ve said all along that free-to-play titles are very challenging, whether that’s in mobile or PC or console,” Zelnick explained. “But live service, I would say that’s too broad a brush, because live services are extremely successful. The bulk of our business is represented by live services and what we call recurrent consumer spend. It’s the vast majority of our business today.” He added: “The business basically runs on live services, punctuated by, we hope, some huge releases.”

sources.title: Take-Two boss isn't worried about GTA 6 players jailbreaking PS5 consoles and modding it
sources.text: FiveM is the go-to resource for such things There aren't many sure bets in video games, but GTA 6 is definitely one of the few you can guarantee will be a big launch. The powers that be looking after Rockstar 's long-awaited sequel are so confident, the prospect of players modding their games to circumvent the studio's paid-for services doesn't scare them whatsoever. Strauss Zelnick, CEO of Take-Two , addressed the issue during a shareholder Q&A. "Our purchase of FiveM reflected our support of certain consumers' desires to engage as a creator with our intellectual property," he says. "We've allowed modding in many of our other games. We're just not religious on the topic. The FiveM business is a profitable business for us." FiveM is a custom multiplayer framework for GTA 5. It has a sibling platform called RedM for Red Dead Redemption 2 , and Rockstar bought out the team behind both in 2023. Other, similar portals have since been shut down because FiveM is essentially the 'official' resource for such things. With GTA 6, there'll likely be a rash of other sites and forums to help people modify the game in some way. They'll piggyback off existing methods of jailbreaking the console. Zelnick isn't phased, because he's aware the crime sandbox is going to bring in plenty of money globally. "The mission of this company is to create the best entertainment on Earth and bring it to consumers around the world," he states. "If we do that right, the monetization takes care of itself, and I think that you're going to see that from us in this fiscal year and in future fiscal years." Whatever the critical consensus of the sixth Grand Theft Auto winds up being, I sincerely doubt anyone involved will need to worry too much about their bottom line, even if a few players manage to duck out of paying for any kind of microtransactions. sources.title: 'I think we'd accidentally created the most hardcore extraction game of all time:' EVE Vanguard is taking hard-won playtest lessons into a '24/7 Alpha'
sources.text: It's not early access, not yet. Super-early access. Tomorrow, November 10, EVE Online is releasing a new expansion, Fractured Skies , and companion FPS EVE Vanguard is going into something Fenris Creations is calling a 24/7 alpha. Formal early access on Steam is coming late next year, but you can buy the game and play it through EVE's own client⁠ —and it won't go away like prior playtests. Tomorrow will also see Vanguard start to fulfill its promise as a linked game to EVE Online⁠—completing contracts in the multiplayer FPS will create military campaign opportunities players can find and act on in EVE—marking the return of a dream Fenris (formerly CCP Games) has pursued since the ill-fated PS3 shooter, Dust 514 . I sat down with Vanguard game director Scott Davis and EVE design director Greg Hennessey to talk about what's coming tomorrow and further down the line. From a pure gameplay perspective, Davis told me that NPC AI and new player onboarding are the biggest improvements in Vanguard since its last playtest . The NPC enemies inhabiting Vanguard's levels just weren't challenging enough, and while it's easy to make them better shots, the problem was more one of tactical depth. "We had a lot of people bounce off the game pretty hard in July," Davis said of the other issue, Vanguard's new player experience. "I think we'd accidentally created the most hardcore extraction game of all time, because we had some awkward intricacies to how weapon upgrading and healing worked in the game." There will be more direct tutorializing to address this in tomorrow's Alpha, and a lot of thought has also gone into how Vanguard introduces its modes to players. New players will be introduced through a full co-op/PvE mode, which will then unlock the PvEvP from the last playtest. The final mode sounds the most exciting and unique, though: Davis described it as a PvP-first "3v3v3 procedurally generated labyrinth, where you just go in and only one team can get out alive." That sounds sick, and reminds me a bit of Marathon's Cryo Archive pinnacle activity. I'm encouraged by the variety of playstyle options Vanguard is offering: Marathon seems to have ultimately been sunk by its pure focus on hardcore PvP, while Vanguard might have an advantage attracting and holding a healthy playerbase with such varied modes. The back of the box pitch for Vanguard is that what happens in the FPS will impact EVE Online's one-of-a-kind digital economy, and vice versa. I keep saying it's like the jocks (FPS guys) teaming up with the nerds ( spreadsheet EVE guys), and people generally smile politely when I do. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. The 24/7 alpha is coming with a first version of that interoperability, with mission completion unlocking mining and combat activities in EVE Online. The next big step in this connection is planned for the second quarter of 2027. At that point, Fenris plans for Vanguard players to be able to declare allegiance with one of the four main empires in EVE, then have their mission progress contribute to the Military Campaign and Conquest systems introduced in EVE's latest two expansions. Davis sees the empire allegiance system as a major step by Vanguard toward EVE's style of emergent player behavior. One thing he's looking forward to: Vanguard players adopting faction heraldry on their characters, and the sorts of Arc Raiders moments it may foment out in the wild. Maybe you hold fire on a stranger in PvEvP mode because you recognize you're both aligned with the same faction. Alternately, maybe you go out of your way to hunt down a player because they're aligned with an opposing empire. I was curious if linking the two games had presented any technical difficulties, but both Davis and Hennessey told me it's been surprisingly smooth sailing. "We've sent up many flares ourselves before, but we haven't really had many messages back," Davis told me. "And I wouldn't call it a technical hurdle, because everyone's been working really hard and they know how to do it. But I think that there will be a champagne popping moment of getting those first messages back from EVE Online." Hennessey, meanwhile, said it's less an issue of connecting the two games. Rather, he pointed out that making a game is hard, making two is twice as hard, and that these two games of very different genres have to align with and compliment each other. But I hope it pays off, because this vision of two, nested live games changing and influencing each other in real time is like nothing else out there. Produzido por Rebellion, o estúdio por trás de Sniper Elite e Zombie Army, Atomfall desafiará você a desvendar o sombrio mistério do que realmente aconteceu. Uma releitura impressionante da aclamada obra-prima de RPG e o início narrativo da Trilogia Erdrick. Há muitos anos, o grande herói Ortega despediu-se da esposa e do filho ao partir em uma jornada para derrotar o vilão Baramos, o arquidemônio. Ortega falhou em sua missão, e Baramos ainda ameaça o mundo. Desfira golpes devastadores, esconda-se nas sombras, empunhe armas explosivas e faça os vilões provarem do próprio veneno. Revide, descubra a verdade e enfrente uma ameaça ainda mais mortal do que você. Destaque-se e acompanhe sua jornada com cartões colecionáveis deslumbrantes que celebram seu progresso. Entre na batalha em partidas de vários jogadores de 50 vs. 50 em mapas enormes. Escolha uma das 14 missões na infantaria, os tipos de unidades de reconhecimento e armadura, cada uma equipada com armas, veículos e equipamentos diferentes. Jogue como oficial, batedor, artilheiro, médico, engenheiro, comandante de tanque e muito mais para vivenciar todos os aspectos dos combates da Segunda Guerra Mundial. Enfrente novos inimigos enquanto desvenda os mistérios das antigas civilizações de Nosgoth e revele os planos que estão por trás da corrupção dos Pilares. Em um futuro distante, onde todos os recursos da Terra se esgotaram, estar vivo já é um pecado por si só. Condenado a uma pena de prisão de um milhão de anos, você precisa sobreviver a missões letais para ter qualquer esperança de liberdade. Morra na prisão ou viva no combate. A escolha é sua. Use Thorn, sua arma mais confiável, para dominar o campo de batalha. sources.text: Owlcat Games has revealed a release date for its tactical role-playing sequel Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy. The game arrives 28th January, 2027 on PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S/X. A Switch 2 release date will be provided "at a later date", a press release says. Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy follows the good work laid down by Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader a couple of years ago. "Rogue Trader nails the 40k setting and provides an appropriately massive narrative filled with meaty tactical combat, though some bugs and poor performance hold it back," wrote Caeyln Ellis in Eurogamer's Warhammer 40,000 Rogue Trade review . Dark Heresy changes things by casting you as an Inquisitor and tasking you with hunting down heretics and purging the world of dark influences, as one is wont to do in the 41st century, it seems. And developer Owlcat has apparently overhauled many of the systems underpinning the adventure. There's a beta that's been running for a while that offers a complete first Act to try, and it's accessible if you buy a Founders edition of the game. This beta, incidentally, disappears 7th January, when Owlcat prepares the game for launch. Meanwhile, Owlcat is making a substantially different RPG based around the popular Expanse license - a game that's much more closely inspired by Mass Effect . That project recently recruited the help of former Dragon Age writer David Gaider , and it will no doubt hope to fill a much-lamented hole created recently by the cancellation of Mass Effect 5 .

sources.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's High-Quality Visuals Have Players Second-Guessing Decades of Memories
sources.text: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake gives Link's first 3D adventure a new coat of paint, but some of its details have players second-guessing the reality they thought they once knew. You don't have to be a Zelda expert to know what fairies look like in the original Ocarina of Time. Navi is an icon, which means most people who have ever even thought about touching one of the games in Nintendo's beloved fantasy franchise know that Link's little guide is little more than a glowing ball with wings – or so they thought. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time brought more than just a fancy new tunic for Link when it made the leap to Switch 2 last week. A few close-up shots early in the adventure make one shocking fact clear: The fairies of Kokiri Forest aren't orbs of light – they're fuzzy . It's the kind of detail the original Nintendo 64 release could have never conveyed made real thanks to the artists at Nintendo and the power of the Switch 2. It's about as small as details come but also recontextualizes how many – myself included – have viewed Ocarina of Time's fairies for the last 28 years. "It appears Fairies are just...Fluffy Balls that emit a light!" one Reddit user said . "It's neither a ball of pure light or a humanoid lil person hidden under a glow. Just...Fluff! Interesting :D And cute!" "Answering the important lore questions like 'is that a sentient puffball or a tiny lady who's so shiny you can only see her aura,'" another fan commented . Zelda lore is packed with details that fans have obsessed over for decades, so a revelation like this is kind of groundbreaking. Was it always Nintendo's intention for the fairies to be tiny talking puffballs? Probably not, and if you prefer the pure light orb fairies they'll always be there, too, but fans at least seem to have taken to the change after weekend one. @TAHK0 This is the best thing that’s ever happened to me Fairies are far from the only characters making players question their childhood memories. One that more people have realized pre-remake has to do with the attire of Hyrule guards. Don't worry, if it looked to you like they were wearing some pretty standard fantasy knight armor, you'll be happy to know that is exactly what they're wearing in 2026. "He's wearing f**king jorts?????" one player questioned . "Yes and he looks great in it," another replied . So far my favorite part of the Ocarina of Time Remake is that the guards are wearing booty jorts https://t.co/kjj8kYzORf "I like to believe that all the guards are forced to wear jorts under penalty of death, purely because Zelda decrees it so," another Reddit user suggested . "It’s a really nice detail they added in the remake." Unlike the fairies, it does seem like jorts were standard issue for Zelda's royal guard back in the day. It's just that it's easier to tell that now thanks to the Ocarina of Time remake's Switch 2 graphics. It's made for some funny reactions online, but not all of the new details are quite as charming as jort-wearing knights. Boundary Break host Shesez, who offers out-of-bounds perspectives on video games, got up close and personal with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's creepiest enemies: the ReDeads. In the N64 game, these mummified zombie grapplers were scary enough thanks to their empty eye sockets. On Switch 2, they still look eyeless – at least at a first glance. Get close (but not too close) enough for a good look, zoom in, and you'll see the developers were nice enough to give ReDead's soulless eyeballs behind their masks. Thanks, Nintendo! "That's 100% human skull behind that mask," one person said . The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launched last week for Switch 2 and has been picked apart (complimentary) by the internet in just a few days. Dataminers have found potential hints for what could be some exciting new content . Speedrunners have found some game-changing glitches that have produced some hilarious results . Meanwhile, as players get used to their new jump button, Link is going through it . For more, you can read IGN's review of the game here , or check out our look at the biggest changes from the original 1998 game. Be sure to check out our expanding Ocarina of Time remake walkthrough for comprehensive guides on each main quest area and dungeon, plus where to get Early Heart Pieces, Early Gold Skulltulas , and Early Item Bag Expansions . If you're looking for more, don't miss our complete guides to All Pieces of Heart , All Gold Skulltulas , and All Empty Bottles . Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

sources.title: The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake já roda a 60 FPS e ganha até multiplayer no PC
sources.text: O remake de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, lançado recentemente para Nintendo Switch 2, já está sendo executado em computadores por meio de emuladores. Poucas horas depois da estreia oficial, usuários conseguiram inicializar o jogo no PC, embora a experiência inicial fosse marcada por problemas gráficos, travamentos e desempenho instável. A situação, no entanto, mudou rapidamente. Apenas um dia depois das primeiras tentativas, atualizações dos emuladores Lichii e Eglantine já permitem executar o clássico da Nintendo a até 60 quadros por segundo (FPS), com melhorias significativas na qualidade visual e na estabilidade. Além disso, modders também já trabalham para trazer suporte para multiplayer ao game nos computadores. Até o momento, a Nintendo não comentou sobre o assunto, mas a situação pode levar a movimentações legais da companhia. De acordo com informações do DSOGaming , o emulador Lichii conseguiu corrigir boa parte dos problemas gráficos identificados no primeiro dia de testes. Regiões como a área inicial do jogo e a Árvore Deku já podem ser executadas a 60 FPS, contra os 20 a 30 FPS registrados nas primeiras tentativas. Relatos publicados por usuários também apontam resultados ainda melhores em algumas configurações. Um jogador afirmou ter conseguido executar o remake em 4K e 60 FPS estáveis, sem os principais problemas visuais observados anteriormente, embora pequenos travamentos e congelamentos ainda aconteçam. Outro teste, compartilhado na comunidade do emulador Eglantine, utilizou um processador Ryzen 7 5700X e uma placa de vídeo RTX 5070. O jogador conseguiu avançar até a obtenção da Espada Kokiri em um novo arquivo, mas ainda encontrou problemas de cintilação de texturas, iluminação e dessincronização de áudio em determinadas cenas. Parte da evolução aconteceu graças a mudanças específicas no funcionamento dos emuladores. O Lichii, que é baseado no Eglantine, recebeu correções para problemas que provocavam flashes brancos na tela, cenas completamente pretas e falhas na exibição da vegetação. Os desenvolvedores também trabalharam em otimizações de desempenho, incluindo melhorias no carregamento e armazenamento de shaders. Entre as mudanças estão o reaproveitamento de pipelines gráficos já compilados e a execução de determinadas tarefas em segundo plano durante a inicialização do jogo. O repositório do Eglantine mostra que a equipe publicou diferentes versões experimentais voltadas especificamente à compatibilidade com Ocarina of Time. Como resultado, o progresso tem sido bastante rápido, embora ainda existam limitações que podem variar conforme o hardware e a versão utilizada. Além de melhorar o desempenho do remake no PC, a comunidade de modders já começou a trabalhar em outro recurso: um modo multiplayer. Um vídeo publicado nesta segunda-feira (9) mostra uma versão preliminar da modificação em funcionamento no emulador Lichii, permitindo que jogadores compartilhem a aventura no clássico da Nintendo. O projeto ainda está em desenvolvimento e não possui previsão de lançamento. A expectativa é que a modificação também seja compatível com a versão não oficial do jogo para PC, embora isso ainda dependa de testes e ajustes dos responsáveis pelo projeto. O remake também chamou atenção por uma demonstração envolvendo tecnologias de upscaling. O canal ElAnalistaDeBits publicou uma comparação mostrando como o NVIDIA DLSS pode melhorar a qualidade da imagem do jogo em relação ao AMD FSR 1.0 utilizado originalmente. A demonstração utiliza uma técnica de injeção de DLSS via HDMI, em vez de alterar diretamente o funcionamento interno do jogo. Na comparação, a tecnologia da NVIDIA reduz efeitos de cintilação e melhora a definição de elementos da imagem. Vale lembrar que o Nintendo Switch 2 possui suporte ao DLSS, tecnologia que também já aparece em jogos de outras desenvolvedoras para o console. Mesmo assim, a Nintendo optou pelo FSR 1.0 em Ocarina of Time, uma escolha que chamou atenção diante das possibilidades oferecidas pelo hardware. A chegada do remake aos computadores com modificações também acontece em meio a uma nova onda de avanços na comunidade de emulação do Switch 2. Segundo os relatos, os arquivos do jogo começaram a circular antes do lançamento, após cópias físicas chegarem antecipadamente a alguns consumidores. Pouco depois da divulgação do método, outros jogos exclusivos, como Mario Kart World, também começaram a inicializar em emuladores para PC e até mesmo em dispositivos da Apple. A Nintendo não comentou oficialmente sobre o caso, mas já estaria tomando medidas contra possíveis brechas utilizadas nesse processo. O aplicativo SmileBASIC 4, apontado como uma das portas de entrada para a exploração do sistema, foi removido da eShop. No passado, a empresa também tomou medidas legais contra desenvolvedores de emuladores em uma situação parecida. Após arquivos de Zelda Tears of the Kingdom vazarem antes do lançamento, a companhia iniciou movimentações contra o Yuzu em 2024 por pirataria . Logo, não seria surpreendente ver novas medidas contra ferramentas como Lichii e Eglantine. Em seu site, a Nintendo também deixa claro que é contra o uso de emuladores. A empresa vê os softwares como prejudiciais ao seu modelo de negócio. “Os emuladores não autorizados permitem que certos jogos sejam utilizados de formas não previstas originalmente pelos criadores e incentivam a utilização de cópias não autorizadas (ou seja, pirateadas) dos jogos”, diz a empresa. “Logo, os emuladores têm um impacto negativo na experiência de jogo dos usuários, nos investimentos realizados pelos criadores para desenvolver e publicar jogos únicos e inovadores e, assim, na indústria dos videogames em geral.” E aí, qual a sua opinião sobre o assunto? Weâve shared a creative history with Jeremy going back to Marvel, and weâre eager to see the perspective he brings to DCâs next chapter. Weâre excited to return to what drew us to this job in the first place, which is telling the stories we love, including the next chapter of Clark and Lexâs journey in Man of Tomorrow .â VarietyÂ reports that the pair will be replaced by Marvel veteran Jeremy Latcham, who has credits onÂ Guardians of the Galaxy ,Â Avengers , and Spider-Man films. âJeremy brings a deep reverence for DC and its passionate fanbase, recognizing that they are the very foundation of this storied, multigenerational brand,â said Skydance Motion Picture Group co-chairs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein. âUnder his leadership, every film and television show will be ushered from start to finish through the prism of the legions of fans who love and champion it. Jeremyâs track record exemplifies the excellence he will bring to building out DC and the many beloved characters within it.â The shake-up is pretty unexpected given Gunn and Safran’s quest to get the DC cinematic universe on track had only really just begun. The pair formed DC Studios in 2022, and kicked off a new movie continuity for DC heroes with last year’s acclaimedÂ Superman . This year’sÂ Supergirl was not quite as well received and performed poorly at the box office .Â Clayface , a body horror film about the Batman villain of the same name, was released last month. On the TV side,Â Lanterns and Peacemaker were both received very well after debuting on HBO Max, though the DC Universe’s choices for some early projects had drawn a fair bit of criticism for focusing on obscure characters instead of major players like Batman and Wonder Woman. The People v. Gorilla GroddÂ is an upcoming mockumentary series starring Skyler Gisondo as Jimmy Olson after he debuted as the comic relief character in Superman . Gunn is still attached to next year’sÂ Man of Tomorrow , which he wrote and directed, but both he and Safran “will return full time to creative work” after years of overseeing the DCU’s direction. Update, 11/9/26, 1:15 p.m. Eastern:Â Gunn has released a statement on his Instagram account, confirming he is still working with DC on bothÂ Man of Tomorrow and another project he’s writing on. He leaves it open-ended on whether or not he’ll continue working with the company, saying “we’ll see where it goes after that.” Thanks to all of you who have supported me and Peter in our time as the heads of DC Studios. When I was a kid growing up in Manchester, Missouri, I used to write and draw my own comics with a mix of DC Comics characters and my own characters. Having full access to these characters to do whatever we wanted has been a dream come true. I didn’t know if I wanted this job when it was offered to me, but I just couldn’t pass up the unique opportunity. I’m glad I took the job. There have been so many highs along the way – releasing Superman and Clayface, making Peacemaker, reading the scripts to The People Vs, the entire process of Man of Tomorrow, which thus far has been the best filmmaking experience of my life, and numerous other moments. The highest of the highs have been all the talented and wonderful people I’ve worked with and grown to love: the DC Studios crew, our talented collaborators, our casts and crews, and the boisterous and hilarious fans. And the best part of all has been working with Peter Safran, the smartest and most competent person I know. You’ve been the best partner a person could ask for, and, more so, a truly good friend. But what only the closest people to me have known over the past four years is my time at DC Studios has been trying, to say the least. I dislike the at-times corporate nature of the job (thanks to Peter for taking the brunt of that). I’m always a very hard worker, but as a filmmaker I would at least get to take short breaks to unwind, and I’ve stolen even that time from both myself and my loved ones over the past four years (Jenn, I love you and I’m sorry and you don’t need to feel guilty for being the happiest of all people that I’m no longer doing this job). And the thing my ADHD hyperfocus has had the most difficulty with has been dividing my time between projects I’m incredibly passionate about and the ones I’m not so much and all the things I have to do as a studio head. So, yes, I will miss the people around me, and I will miss being the co-caretaker of these great characters, but I’m also incredibly relieved and excited to get back to pure filmmaking. That’s not to say Peter and 1 are immediately done with DC or superheroes. We have Man of Tomorrow out this summer. And we’ve just been engaged on another DC project which I’m writing, and we’ll see where it goes after that. And, of course, the characters we set up will live on. sources.text: James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as co-heads of DC Studios and will be replaced by former Marvel executive Jeremy Latcham James Gunn and DC Studios co-CEO Peter Safran are stepping down as the heads of DC Studios and will be replaced by former Marvel Studios executive Jeremy Latcham. Per The Hollywood Reporter , Gunn and Safran are out of the job from December 1, 2026. That's just over four years after the pair were appointed to the post. In that time, DC Studios has released three movies ( Superman , Supergirl and Clayface ) and four TV shows (Creature Commandos, Peacemaker season 2 , The Penguin and Lanterns ). Projects currently in the pipeline include Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow , Jimmy Olsen series The People v. Gorilla Grodd, Creature Commandos season 2, and Elseworlds movie The Batman: Part II . “Four years ago, we set out to unite DC under one creative vision," Gunn and Safran said in a statement. "In that time, we helped restore Superman to the heart of DC, while opening new doors and telling new stories in film and television with Peacemaker, Creature Commandos, Lanterns and Clayface. "We’re immensely proud of the team that turned that ambition into something real, including the actors, crews and executives we had the opportunity to collaborate with. "We’ve shared a creative history with Jeremy going back to Marvel, and we’re eager to see the perspective he brings to DC’s next chapter," Gunn and Safran said of their replacement at DC Studios. "We're excited to return to what drew us to this job in the first place, which is telling the stories we love, including the next chapter of Clark and Lex’s journey in Man of Tomorrow." In a separate, longer statement on Threads , Gunn said he's "incredibly relieved and excited to get back to pure filmmaking" and noted "the characters we set up will live on". Latcham is Marvel Studios' former senior VP of production and development, and was Kevin Feige's right-hand man at the company for a time, with credits on Iron Man, The Avengers, Guardians of the Galaxy and Spider-Man: Homecoming. As with Gunn and Safran, Latcham will oversee DC's film, TV and animation slate. "James and Peter launched a new era for DC Studios and led it through a period of real transformation, resetting the foundation and building a slate we’re incredibly proud of," Skydance bosses David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz said in a statement . "We're grateful for their passion, contributions and commitment to this legendary brand." Subscribe for a weekly digest of the movie and TV news that matters, direct to your inbox. From first-look trailers, interviews, reviews and explainers, we’ve got you covered. What the future now holds for DC is now less clear than ever. While several projects from the Gunn and Safran era are still in the pipeline, many were critical of Gunn and Safran's decision not to launch their shared universe with big-hitters like Batman and Wonder Woman, and instead focus on lesser-explored characters like Supergirl and Clayface. Could a creative reboot be on the cards, despite Gunn's Superman movies still being an ongoing concern? We'll soon find out. Man of Tomorrow releases on July 9, 2027.
